body:
There are a bunch of limitations to the way it works - see https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setforegroundwindow#remarks

> An application cannot force a window to the foreground while the user is working with another window. Instead, Windows flashes the taskbar button of the window to notify the user.

That's informative and unfortunate. Especially annoying is:

> It is possible for a process to be denied the right to set the foreground window even if it meets these conditions.

In theory my desired use case should be able to meet these conditions. I'm debugging a turn-based multiplayer game, and when running multiple instances, I want to swap focus when it switches to another players turn. But, if I'm reading it right, it seems like the window currently in focus needs to ask to put the other window in focus? Not sure how you'd go about getting the window handle, though. Any suggestions on that would be appreciated, but ultimately it's not that important to my project.

I think this might deserve a note in the documentation that `grab_focus` essentially does not work in Win11. 
EDIT: I'm assuming this is only relevant to Win11, but I don't actually know if it's also a problem on 10 or before.

Also `has_focus` does still return the wrong value. Don't know if windows itself is reporting it as in focus or the engine is just assuming it is since `grab_focus` was called and it hasn't received a focus lost notification.
